vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-102554
vulnerability.description: Guava eagerly allocates an array sized from the stream when deserializing CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet or MapMakerInternalMap, so a crafted Java serialization stream causes OutOfMemoryError (DoS). Affects 4.0 through 33.7.1; fixed in 33.7.2.

statements.impact_statement: SOURCE: the finding is guava 33.6.0-jre in Maven's own lib directory (/usr/share/maven/lib), which comes with the base image maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-17. It is not a dependency of any project buildenv builds. REACHABILITY: CVE-2026-102554 is a denial of service (OutOfMemoryError) that needs Java object deserialization (ObjectInputStream) of a crafted stream holding a Guava CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet or MapMakerInternalMap. Maven uses guava internally (Sisu/Guice wiring, the resolver) and does not deserialize Java serialization streams from network or project input: POMs, settings and repository metadata are XML, and artifacts are read as files. So no adversary-controlled serialized stream reaches the vulnerable readObject path. Impact would be availability-only (a crash of the Maven process during a build). NO UPSTREAM FIX EXISTS: Maven 3.9.16 (latest release at time of writing) ships guava 33.6.0; guava 33.7.2 is only on Maven's unreleased 3.9.x branch (3.9.17-SNAPSHOT). Replacing the jar in Maven's lib dir by hand changes the base image's tested contents. DROP TRIGGER: a maven:3.9 image with Maven 3.9.17 or later (guava >= 33.7.2); then rebuild and delete this statement and GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94. TTL: .github/vex-ttl.json. Tracked in #180.
